blockers.theDECISIVEDEMONSTRATION: I replaced delivery.v4's DL-CLOSED-1 with delivery.v3's REJECTED text -- the exact catch-all formulation that earned blocker IR-V3-B1 and that refuses 100 per cent of the live data -- and left everything else untouched. THE RUN EXITS 0 WITH FINDINGS: 0. The checker implements the record/map property from its own hardcoded CM_KEYS / PC_KEYS / AC_KEYS and _reachable_objects and never reads the artifact's statement of it. An instrument retained beside a repair, which passes the unrepaired text, is not evidence of the repair.
theSAMEHOLESELSEWHERE_ALLMEASURED: DL-DOM-1's statement replaced by its negation ('no registry constrains any position') -- exit 0, 0 findings.
DL-ORD-1 reversed to say a consumer SORTS rather than REJECTS -- exit 0, 0 findings.
DL-INJ-1's detector claim reversed to assert it finds all three channels, which is the precise overclaim this version repaired -- exit 0, 0 findings.
PLATFORM-ID-DOMAIN-V1.memberCount changed from 8 to 99 -- exit 0. memberCount is never read by any gate.

a real platform member replaced with the invented 'freebsd-x86_64-INVENTED' -- exit 0. Likewise an invented relation member and an invented deficiency member. The checker builds the TRUE registries from live delivery.v2 and fact-plane.v1 bytes and uses them for admission, but NEVER compares the artifact's PUBLISHED member lists against them -- and the published lists are the normative content an implementer would build from.

AbsentCapability.relationIds[] REBOUND from the relation registry to the deficiency vocabulary -- exit 0. gate_domain_census flattens all boundPositions into one multiset and compares that; the position-to-registry assignment is never checked.

the artifact's own verbatim quotation of freeze section 6 law 2 replaced with a fabrication -- exit 0. FREEZE_ANCHORS holds the CHECKER's copy and verifies it against the live freeze; the ARTIFACT's copy is never compared to anything.

the minted domain label changed to 'opensip.SOMETHING-ELSE.v1' in closedDomainVocabulary, and independently in recipe.oneLine -- exit 0 both times, even though the checker's own DOMAIN constant still says 'opensip.capability-manifest.v1'. Artifact and instrument may disagree about the one string this document mints and the run stays green.
DCM-1 and DCM-2's profileId labels swapped, so each vector claims the other profile while its committed manifest's `profile` field says otherwise, contradicting DL-CUST-3 -- exit 0.

a recordedInputs digest replaced with sixty-four 'f' characters -- exit 0. Worse, gate_digest_accountability builds its `recorded` set FROM the artifact's own recordedInputs, so a fabricated digest laundered through that block accounts for itself.
blockers.whatWouldCLOSEIT: gates that compare the artifact's DECLARATIONS to their declared sources: published registry members and memberCounts against the live registries the checker already builds; each boundPosition against the registry it is filed under; recordedInputs digests against the files; the artifact's quoted freeze text against the live freeze; and at minimum a content anchor on DL-CLOSED-1, DL-DOM-1 and DL-ORD-1 so that the normative sentences cannot be replaced by their negations under a green run.
blockers.whatDoesNOTCloseIt: more mutations of the checker's own logic. All 17 existing selftest mutations perturb the CHECKER and require the run to fail. None perturbs the ARTIFACT. That is precisely why the suite is green on a document whose central property has been replaced by the rejected one.

nonBlockingInstrumentObservations.finding: UNHANDLED EXCEPTION ON A MALFORMED committedBytesHex. Setting DCM-1-core.committedBytesHex's first byte to 07 makes decode() raise EncErr('trailing bytes after a complete CVE1 value') out of gate_vectors with a traceback instead of a named finding. It FAILS CLOSED -- the process still exits non-zero -- but it violates the run's own promise that 'each finding names its position', and a traceback is not a diagnostic. A try/except around the decode raising DV4-VECTOR would fix it.

DIAGNOSTIC LABEL INVERSION IN gate_derivation. Both run.eq calls there pass the ARTIFACT's value as `got` and the measured truth as `want`, so the message reads 'recomputed <artifact value>, artifact publishes <true value>' -- backwards from every other call site. The comparison is correct and fails correctly; only the message misleads. I hit it on a real mutation.

gate_digest_accountability RE-READS THE SUBJECT FROM DISK with (COOP / SUBJECT).read_text() rather than using the bytes verify_pins() already hash-verified. Every other gate works from the verified parse. Harmless in a normal run but it is a time-of-check/time-of-use inconsistency in the one gate whose whole purpose is to leave nothing untrusted.

THE SCALAR CENSUS IS TRANSCRIBED, NOT DERIVED. BOUND_SCALARS and OPEN_SCALARS are hardcoded literal lists; CM_KEYS / PC_KEYS / AC_KEYS are never used to construct them, and selfMeasurement.reachableScalarTypePositions is recomputed at line 1563 as len(bound) + len(declaredOPEN) from the ARTIFACT's own lists. So the census gate compares the artifact's list to the checker author's transcription of the same list, and nothing in the run can discover a NEW reachable position. This is the measurement behind the artifact-side observation OBS-1.

THE SELFTEST'S REACH IS NARROWER THAN ITS FRAMING SUGGESTS. Its own header says 'each mutation must fail the run, and must fail for its OWN reason', which it delivers. But all 17 mutations perturb the CHECKER. The artifact declares this honestly at knownLimitationsV4 -- 'It does not show that no fifteenth mutation passes' -- and that honesty is why this is an observation and not a second blocker. The author's report that the first selftest run failed three of its own mutations and exposed three real checker defects is consistent with the code I read: the ADMITTED sentinel is a deliberately unmatchable string with a comment naming SKIP_DOMAIN as what found the defect.

theSection78QuestionAnsweredConcretely.question: How much of a green run is agreement between the artifact and an instrument built from the same reading?
theSection78QuestionAnsweredConcretely.answer: The green run splits cleanly into two halves that deserve different credit. The RECOMPUTATION half is genuine independent evidence against the ARITHMETIC and I confirmed all of it from the prose with my own encoder: ids, byte strings, lengths, PlanIds, preimages, counts, censuses, the derivation replay. Those cannot be faked by shared reading because SHA-256 does not care who wrote the encoder. The DECLARATION half is pure agreement: the record/map property, the value-domain property, the ordering property, the scalar census, the registry contents and the minted domain label all exist twice -- once as prose in the artifact and once as Python constants in the checker, both written by the same lane from the same reading -- and the run only ever compares the Python to itself or to live data, never to the artifact's prose. That is why replacing the artifact's central property with the rejected one leaves the run green.
namingWhatTheInstrumentWouldNOTCatch: any change to a normative sentence: DL-CLOSED-1, DL-DOM-1, DL-ORD-1, DL-ORD-2, DL-INJ-1 and every gate `statement` can be edited, weakened or reversed without a finding.
any change to a published registry's members, memberCount or source prose.
any re-assignment of a bound position to the wrong registry.
any falsification of a quotation the artifact attributes to another document, including the freeze quotation its own ordering ruling rests on.
any change to a recordedInputs digest, which additionally launders itself through the accountability gate.
any change to the minted domain label as the ARTIFACT states it.
any cross-document claim, such as idIsUNCHANGEDfromDeliveryV3 or the candidatePredecessor's sha256, except where a changed 64-hex literal happens to trip the accountability ledger.
every `why`, `separates`, `rationale` and narrative field in the document, which is the large majority of its 220,882 bytes.
and, structurally, ANY defect shared between the artifact's reading and the checker author's reading, because they are the same reading.
theSection78QuestionAnsweredConcretely.soWHATISAGREENRUNWORTH: It is strong evidence that the numbers are right and weak evidence that the document is right. Used as the former it is excellent. Used as the latter it would be the mistake section 7.8 names. This review therefore grounds its verdict on independent recomputation and cites the green run only as corroboration.

couldIMakeTheCheckerPassOnAWrongArtifact.answer: YES, EASILY, AND IN MANY WAYS THAT MATTER.
couldIMakeTheCheckerPassOnAWrongArtifact.theSharpestSingleCASE: restore delivery.v3's rejected DL-CLOSED-1 text -- the exact bytes of blocker IR-V3-B1 -- and the run still reports EXIT 0, FINDINGS: 0.
couldIMakeTheCheckerPassOnAWrongArtifact.andTHEIMPORTANTQUALIFIER: every one of these is a defect in the INSTRUMENT's coverage, not a defect I found in the artifact. I hard-compared the artifact's actual published registries against the live sources -- PLATFORM-ID-DOMAIN-V1's eight members against delivery.v2's platformMatrix (5 supported + 2 bestEffort + the aggregate token), the twelve relations and five deficiency values against fact-plane.v1 -- and ALL ARE CORRECT, as are all three memberCounts. The artifact tells the truth; the checker simply would not have noticed if it had not.

nonBlockingObservations.grade: NON-BLOCKING -- THE STRONGEST FINDING IN THIS REVIEW, AND THE ONE A LATER READER IS MOST INVITED TO RE-GRADE
nonBlockingObservations.finding: THE ARTIFACT OVERSTATES WHAT ITS RETAINED INSTRUMENT VERIFIES, AT EXACTLY THE POSITION WHERE ITS OWN PREDECESSOR WAS FAULTED FOR AN OVERSTATEMENT. censusIsEXHAUSTIVE says 'The retained checker recomputes this census from the schema and fails the run if any reachable scalar position is in neither list.' MEASURED FALSE: BOUND_SCALARS and OPEN_SCALARS are hardcoded literal lists never derived from CM_KEYS / PC_KEYS / AC_KEYS, and reachability is not computed anywhere in the program. whatItDoes[5] repeats it as 'including the exhaustiveness of the fourteen-position scalar census', and whatItDoes[8] counts 'bound and open scalar positions' among recomputed values when they are len() of the artifact's own lists.
nonBlockingObservations.whyITMATTERS: the sentence promises protection against precisely the drift it cannot detect. If a successor adds a key to ProviderCapability, adm_closed would use the new key set while the census lists would not gain the new scalar position, and the census gate would stay green with a reachable scalar in neither list.
nonBlockingObservations.whyITISNOTGRADEDABLOCKER: see whyZEROANDNOTONE. The census itself is CORRECT -- I re-derived 2 + 7 + 5 = 14 from the three record key sets independently of both documents -- DL-DOM-1 is sound, no id moves, and this lineage's own prior review graded two comparable evidentiary overclaims non-blocking.
nonBlockingObservations.theONECLAUSEREPAIR: narrow it to what is true: 'the retained checker compares this census against its own independently written list of the same fourteen positions, and fails on disagreement.' Deriving the positions from the declared key sets in the checker would then make the original sentence true.

The artifact files them under digestAccountability case (a).
I did not verify the OBS-V4-1 order-divergence census (10 positions) or the proposal's R-A grammar reproduction, for the same reason.

I spot-checked but did not exhaustively re-derive the prefix-form census. I confirmed the structure of the claim -- predicateA count 5, predicateB count 3, total 8, with all eight positions enumerated by JSON path -- and confirmed the PREFIX_PREDICATE_BLIND mutation's 8-versus-5 behaviour, but I did not independently walk delivery.v2 for every statement matching each predicate.

I did not attempt a full second-preimage argument on step4_theCONVERSEISIMPOSSIBLE; I accepted that reproducing 2222...2222 or 7777...7777 from a real manifest would require breaking SHA-256, and I confirmed the placeholder literals are what the goldens actually carry.

I did not exhaustively enumerate every one of the 17 negative controls' minted values. I independently reproduced NEG-CLOSED-2 (all three ids and all three byte lengths), NEG-CLOSED-3 (both readings, all counts), NEG-DUP-1 (both values), NEG-DUP-2, NEG-PLAT-1 (both ids) and NEG-PLAT-2. The remaining controls I read but did not recompute.

I could not recover delivery.v3's NEG-DUP-2 base manifest or NEG-CLOSED-2's 39-byte absent-half value. My search was 875,781 candidates over a restricted alphabet and short lengths; absence of a hit is not proof they are unrecoverable, only that two independent lanes have now failed to find them.

I did not review the C-2, RETENTION, EVIDENCE or EVALUATION-PROOF surfaces except where delivery.v4 cites them, and I did not re-review delivery.v2's own contents beyond the platformMatrix, installProfiles and capabilityManifestSchema that this artifact depends on.

I did not attempt to prove the absence of a FIFTH injectivity channel. I found one beyond the three claimed and it was already disclosed; the class is not closed and the artifact does not claim it is.

My mutation battery against the instrument was roughly forty constructions. It establishes that wide classes of wrong artifacts pass; it does not enumerate them, and I did not attempt to bound what else passes.
reviewerStatement: I set out to reject both. I could not reject the artifact: every value I recomputed matched, the blocker repair is a sound property rather than an exemption, the law-2 re-grounding is a real improvement whose entailment holds, the fourteen-position census is exhaustive and correct, and the document's self-criticism repeatedly reached my findings before I did -- including the fourth injectivity channel I constructed, which it had already declared. I did reject the instrument, on one blocker: it is a first-rate arithmetic engine that cannot tell whether the document's normative sentences say what they should, and I proved that by restoring the rejected predecessor's blocked text and watching it exit 0. The honest summary of the pair is that the numbers in delivery.v4 are independently confirmed and the prose in delivery.v4 is confirmed by nothing but reading -- mine, now, in addition to its author's.
